scenario.title: Equipment-Specific Measurement Workflow
scenario.initial_description: A wafer is measured using one of several tools. The exact preparation and measurement steps differ by tool, and the engineer records the result after measurement.

reference_workflow.goal: Measure a wafer using the appropriate equipment-specific procedure and record the result.

activities.name: Confirm measurement request and wafer identifier
Check equipment availability and reserve slot
Prepare wafer according to equipment procedure

decisions.condition: Which equipment is required for the requested measurement?
Is the equipment available and qualified?

automation_opportunities.rationale: Equipment selection can be recommended from measurement type and wafer condition.
Reservation checks can be automated through system integration.
Output validity can be partially checked using rule-based thresholds or historical patterns.

activities.name: Perform Measurement on Tool A
outputs: Raw measurement data from Tool A

activities.name: Perform Measurement on Tool B
outputs: Raw measurement data from Tool B

activities.name: Perform Measurement on Tool C
outputs: Raw measurement data from Tool C

decisions.condition: Is the measurement result valid and within acceptance criteria?

exceptions.description: Selected tool is unavailable or under maintenance
exceptions.resolution: Reassign to alternative tool or queue for tool availability

exceptions.description: Measurement data is incomplete or corrupted
exceptions.trigger: Raw measurement data fails integrity check
exceptions.resolution: Repeat measurement step or flag for manual inspection
Quarantine wafer and raise non-conformance report

automation_opportunities.rationale: Tool selection can be automated based on real-time tool availability, wafer type, and measurement requirements, reducing manual decision-making and idle time.
constraints: Tool scheduling system must expose availability API
Rules for tool-wafer compatibility must be formalized

automation_opportunities.target: A3a / A3b / A3c - Prepare Wafer for Tool
automation_opportunities.rationale: Preparation steps are tool-specific but recipe-driven and repeatable; tool controllers can auto-load preparation recipes upon wafer registration, reducing manual setup errors.
constraints: Recipes must be digitized and stored in tool controller
Physical wafer loading may still require human intervention

automation_opportunities.rationale: Modern measurement tools can execute measurement sequences autonomously once configured, removing the need for engineer presence during measurement execution.
constraints: Requires compatible tool automation interfaces
Initial calibration verification may need manual sign-off

automation_opportunities.target: A5 - Review and Validate Measurement Result
automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated statistical comparison of raw measurement data against pre-defined acceptance criteria can replace manual review for standard cases, flagging only outliers for human review.
constraints: Acceptance criteria must be formally defined and maintained
Edge cases and novel failure modes may require human judgment

automation_opportunities.rationale: Measurement results can be automatically written to the lab management system directly from tool output, eliminating manual data entry and transcription errors.
constraints: Integration between tool controller and lab management system required
Data format standardization needed across tools

automation_opportunities.rationale: Automated escalation notifications can be triggered immediately upon detection of a fail flag, reducing response time and ensuring consistent escalation paths.
constraints: Escalation rules and responsible parties must be predefined
Human approval may be needed for rework decisions

assumptions: There are at least three distinct measurement tools (Tool A, Tool B, Tool C), each with different preparation and measurement procedures.
Tool selection is based on factors such as availability, wafer type, and measurement specification, though the exact selection criteria are not specified.
Each tool has a defined recipe or protocol that governs preparation and measurement steps.
The engineer is responsible for both preparation and result recording, though tool operation may be partially automated.
A formal acceptance criteria or specification exists against which measurement results are evaluated.
Failed measurements trigger a re-measurement or escalation loop rather than immediate wafer disposal.
The lab management system and tool controllers are separate systems that may or may not currently be integrated.
Measurement results are stored in a centralized system as part of wafer traceability requirements.
